interest: Documents postwar Manchuria's industrial collapse through Takasaki's eyewitness account of looting, Soviet removals, and shrinking Japanese technician retention plans.
overview: This file (U.S. State Department decimal file 894.503193) consists of two diplomatic despatches (Nos. 41 and 43, including carbon copies designated for the U.S. Embassy in Moscow) sent in April 1947 by American Consul General O. Edmund Clubb from Changchun, China, regarding the condition of Japanese industrial installations and the status of retained Japanese technicians in post-war Manchuria. The documents center on detailed assessments by Tatsunosuke Takasaki, former president of the Manchuria Heavy Industry Development Company (Mangyo) and councillor to the Nationalist Government's Northeast Economic Commission. Despatch No. 41 encloses an English translation of Takasaki's address to the Japanese Residents Liaison Conference in Mukden, which details how Soviet dismantlement, widespread mob looting, runaway inflation, and civil conflict reduced the operational capacity of Manchuria's estimated $12 billion industrial plant by up to 90%, necessitating a reduction in retained Japanese technicians from 25,000 to 3,000. Despatch No. 43 encloses Clubb's memorandum of a confidential conversation with Takasaki on April 12, 1947, detailing rail breakdown, stockpiled coal and lack of inter-departmental coordination at Fushun and Penhsihu, and Takasaki's proposal that American capital and engineering experts be enlisted to manage and rehabilitate Manchurian continental industry.

subfiles.about: Covering despatch transmitting an English translation of a speech by Tatsunosuke Takasaki on the condition of Manchurian industrial plants and retained Japanese technicians.
subfiles.from: O. Edmund Clubb, American Consul General, Harbin (at Changchun)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 41: Clubb forwards Takasaki's account that Soviet removals, looting, inflation, and conflict cut Manchuria's industrial capacity to about 10% of its $12 billion value, reducing needed retained Japanese technicians from 25,000 to 3,000.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 41 from O. Edmund Clubb to Secretary of State on Japanese Plant and Technicians in Manchuria
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: English translation of Tatsunosuke Takasaki's address at the Japanese Residents Liaison Conference discussing industrial damage in Manchuria and the employment of Japanese technicians.
subfiles.summary: Translated Tohoku Doho speech: Takasaki urges retained Japanese to appreciate Chinese protection and Chinese authorities to treat them as specialists, explaining that Soviet removals ($2 billion), looting, transport breakdowns, and inflation cut Manchuria's $12 billion industrial value to about 10%, leaving only 3,000 technicians needed instead of 25,000.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 41: Translation of Speech by Tatsunosuke Takasaki in Tohoku Doho
subfiles.to: Japanese Residents Liaison Conference / Chinese authorities

subfiles.about: Covering despatch forwarding a memorandum of conversation with Tatsunosuke Takasaki regarding Manchuria's deteriorating economy and administrative problems.
subfiles.from: O. Edmund Clubb, American Consul General, Harbin (at Changchun)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 43: Clubb reports Takasaki's view that Chinese Nationalist authorities lack industrial administration experience and coordination, and that American engineers would be more readily accepted than Japanese advice.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 43 from O. Edmund Clubb to Secretary of State on the Economic Situation in Manchuria
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: Record of a confidential interview between O. Edmund Clubb and Tatsunosuke Takasaki discussing industrial paralysis, bureaucratic fragmentation, and the need for American technical assistance in Manchuria.
subfiles.from: O. Edmund Clubb, American Consul General
subfiles.summary: Memo of Clubb's conversation with Takasaki: destruction and looting left only 10% of Manchuria's industrial capacity usable, requiring repatriation of most of 10,000 retained Japanese technicians; transport collapse strands coal at Fushun and Penhsihu, and Takasaki recommends American engineers and capital, recalling Aikawa's plans.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 43: Memorandum of Conversation with Tatsunosuke Takasaki

subfiles.about: Duplicate diplomatic copy of Despatch No. 43 marked for transmittal by the Department of State to the U.S. Embassy in Moscow.
subfiles.from: O. Edmund Clubb, American Consul General, Harbin (at Changchun)
subfiles.summary: Carbon copy of Despatch No. 43 for Moscow, reporting Clubb's interview with Takasaki on Manchuria's economic decline, Nationalist administrative shortcomings, and proposals for American engineering assistance.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 43 from O. Edmund Clubb to Secretary of State (Moscow Embassy Copy)
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C. (for Embassy Moscow)

subfiles.about: Duplicate diplomatic copy of the memorandum of conversation between Clubb and Takasaki designated for transmittal to the U.S. Embassy in Moscow.
subfiles.from: O. Edmund Clubb, American Consul General
subfiles.summary: Moscow copy of the April 1947 Clubb-Takasaki conversation memo: Manchurian industrial capacity down to 10%, repatriation of 7,000 of 10,000 remaining Japanese technicians, transport and coordination breakdowns at Fushun and Penhsihu, and Takasaki's recollection of Aikawa's plans for American capital and engineering.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 43: Memorandum of Conversation with Tatsunosuke Takasaki (Moscow Embassy Copy)
